dedupe_keys.name: identifying and sharing per and polyfluoroalkyl substances hot spot areas and exposures in drinking water

description: Identifying and sharing per-and polyfluoroalkyl substances hot-spot areas and exposures in drinking water is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Sweta Ojha et al. Exposure to per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in drinking water is widely recognized as a public health concern. Decision-makers who are responsible for managing PFAS drinking water risks lack the tools to acquire the information they need. Coverage: not stated; published in 2023. The formats are not stated in the sources read. The data are held in Figshare and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Size stated by the repository: 3482498 Bytes. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence is CC-BY-4.0, taken from DataCite rights of the deposit. Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked, and the coverage and resolution are those of the abstract only. It can support water-network, drainage and hydraulic studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
